s1.syndrome_frame: Cardiac arrest with preceding respiratory distress
salient_findings: Cardiac arrest with pulseless electrical activity as initial rhythm
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) with shortness of breath for 2 days prior to presentation
Return of spontaneous circulation after cardiopulmonary resuscitation and epinephrine administration
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 80s
Last seen healthy by family 4 hours prior to cardiac arrest
Found unresponsive and pulseless in the bathroom
Underwent cardiopulmonary resuscitation with 4 doses of epinephrine intravenously
Endotracheal tube intubation was performed
Return of spontaneous circulation occurred after approximately 10 minutes
Patient has chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
Patient complained of shortness of breath for 2 days prior to presentation
Family member witnessed patient struggling for air before losing consciousness
Initial rhythm was pulseless electrical activity
ECG findings include sinus rhythm at approximately 100 beats per minute, right axis deviation, and prolonged QRS duration

shortlist.label: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease exacerbation
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has COPD and complained of shortness of breath for 2 days prior to presentation

shortlist.label: Pulmonary embolism
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had cardiac arrest and complained of shortness of breath, which are common symptoms of pulmonary embolism

shortlist.label: Myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had cardiac arrest and ECG findings include sinus rhythm at approximately 100 beats per minute and prolonged QRS duration

shortlist.label: Cor pulmonale
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has COPD and right axis deviation on ECG, which is a common finding in cor pulmonale

shortlist.label: Right ventricular failure
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has COPD and ECG findings include prolonged QRS duration and right axis deviation, which are common findings in right ventricular failure

raw.rationale: The patient's history of COPD and complaints of shortness of breath for 2 days prior to presentation, along with the family member witnessing him struggling for air before losing consciousness, suggest that a COPD exacerbation led to the cardiac arrest.

rejected.label: Pulmonary embolism
rejected.why: There is no direct evidence of a pulmonary embolism, such as a reported DVT or sudden onset of symptoms without prior respiratory issues.

rejected.label: Myocardial infarction
rejected.why: Coronary angiography showed no acute occlusions, making myocardial infarction less likely as the primary cause of the cardiac arrest.

rejected.label: Cor pulmonale
rejected.why: While the patient has COPD, which can lead to cor pulmonale, the information provided does not specifically indicate right-sided heart failure due to lung disease as the primary cause of the cardiac arrest.

rejected.label: Right ventricular failure
rejected.why: Although the ECG shows right axis deviation and other signs that could suggest right ventricular strain, the primary issue appears to be related to the patient's COPD exacerbation rather than isolated right ventricular failure.

gold: Right Bundle Branch Block (RBBB) with cardiac arrest due to hypoxemia from COPD exacerbation
